questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the titration above, the average titre that should be used in the calculation is
questions.explanation: Only the concordant titres (24.90 and 25.10 cm³, within 0.2 cm³ of each other) are averaged: (24.90 + 25.10)/2 = 25.00 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the titration above, the number of moles of hydrochloric acid in the average titre is
questions.explanation: Moles = concentration × volume in dm³ = 0.10 × 25.00/1000 = 0.0025 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the titration above, the concentration of the sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution in mol/dm³ is
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂, so moles Na₂CO₃ = 0.0025/2 = 0.00125 in 25.0 cm³; concentration = 0.00125/0.025 = 0.050 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the titration above, the concentration of the sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution in g/dm³ is
questions.explanation: Molar mass of Na₂CO₃ = 2(23) + 12 + 3(16) = 106; 0.050 mol/dm³ × 106 g/mol = 5.30 g/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the titration above, the colour change observed at the end point is from
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is yellow in the alkaline carbonate solution in the flask and turns orange (then red) as the acid from the burette reaches the end point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the titration above, the result of titration 1 was left out when finding the average because
questions.A: the burette was wrongly read from the top of the meniscus
questions.B: the first portion of the solution was not exactly 25.0 cm³
questions.C: too much indicator was added to the first conical flask
questions.D: it was only a rough trial and differs from the others by over 0.2 cm³
questions.explanation: The first titration is a rough run to locate the end point; only titres that agree closely (concordant) are used in the calculation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, the average rate of reaction during the first 20 seconds is
questions.explanation: Rate = volume of gas ÷ time = 30 cm³ ÷ 20 s = 1.5 cm³/s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, the average rate of reaction between 40 s and 60 s is
questions.explanation: Volume produced between 40 s and 60 s = 62 − 50 = 12 cm³; 12/20 = 0.6 cm³/s, slower than at the start.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, the reaction was complete after about
questions.explanation: No more hydrogen was collected after 80 s (the volume stayed at 68 cm³), so the magnesium had all reacted by then.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the experiment above, the rate of reaction decreased with time because
questions.A: the temperature of the acid kept rising
questions.C: hydrogen gas dissolved in the acid
questions.D: the magnesium was gradually used up
questions.explanation: The acid was in excess, so it was the magnesium (the limiting reactant) whose amount and surface fell as the reaction proceeded, giving fewer collisions per second.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the experiment above were repeated with the same mass of magnesium powder instead of ribbon, the final volume of hydrogen would be
questions.A: 68 cm³, collected in a shorter time
questions.B: 68 cm³, collected in a longer time
questions.D: less than 68 cm³, collected more slowly
questions.explanation: The same amount of magnesium gives the same amount of hydrogen; the larger surface area of the powder only makes the reaction faster.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the final volume of hydrogen in the data above, the mass of magnesium used was about (Mg = 24, molar volume at room temperature = 24,000 cm³)
questions.explanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂: 68/24,000 = 0.00283 mol of H₂ came from 0.00283 mol of Mg = 0.00283 × 24 = 0.068 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the strongest reducing agent is
questions.explanation: The most negative electrode potential belongs to the metal that loses electrons most readily; magnesium (−2.37 V) is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the e.m.f. of the cell Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(aq)||Ag⁺(aq)|Ag(s) under standard conditions is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, which of the following reactions will take place spontaneously?
questions.explanation: A metal displaces the ions of any metal with a more positive E°. Copper (+0.34 V) can reduce Ag⁺ (+0.80 V): E°cell = +0.46 V. The other three have negative e.m.f.s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the metal that would protect an iron pipe best when attached to it as a sacrificial anode is
questions.explanation: A sacrificial anode must be more easily oxidised (more negative E°) than iron; magnesium at −2.37 V corrodes in place of the iron. Copper and silver would make the iron corrode faster.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the table above, the e.m.f. of a cell made from the Fe²⁺/Fe and Cu²⁺/Cu half-cells is
questions.explanation: Copper is the cathode: E°cell = 0.34 − (−0.44) = 0.78 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a cell Mg(s)|Mg²⁺(aq)||Cu²⁺(aq)|Cu(s) built from the table above, reduction takes place at
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ ions gain electrons (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu) at the copper electrode, the cathode; magnesium is oxidised at the anode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, the mass of KNO₃ that crystallises out when a saturated solution containing 100 g of water is cooled from 60 °C to 20 °C is
questions.explanation: At 60 °C the solution holds 110 g per 100 g of water; at 20 °C only 32 g can stay dissolved, so 110 − 32 = 78 g crystallises.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, the maximum mass of KNO₃ that will dissolve in 50 g of water at 80 °C is
questions.explanation: Solubility at 80 °C is 169 g per 100 g of water, so 50 g of water dissolves 169/2 = 84.5 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, the solubility of KNO₃ at 20 °C in mol/dm³ is approximately (take 100 g of water as 100 cm³)
questions.explanation: 32 g per 100 cm³ = 320 g/dm³; 320 ÷ 101 = 3.17 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the data above, when 80 g of KNO₃ is stirred with 100 g of water at 40 °C, the mass of solid that remains undissolved is
questions.explanation: Only 64 g can dissolve in 100 g of water at 40 °C, so 80 − 64 = 16 g stays as solid and the solution is saturated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The data above show that the dissolution of KNO₃ in water is
questions.A: exothermic, since solubility rises with temperature
questions.B: neither, since solubility does not change with temperature
questions.C: exothermic, since solubility falls with temperature
questions.D: endothermic, since solubility rises with temperature
questions.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, heating favours the endothermic direction; since more salt dissolves as the temperature rises, dissolving absorbs heat.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A mixture contains iodine crystals, sand and sodium chloride. The correct order of processes for separating the three components is
questions.A: sublimation, then dissolving in water, filtration and evaporation
questions.B: filtration, then sublimation, dissolving and evaporation
questions.C: evaporation, then filtration, sublimation and dissolving
questions.D: dissolving in water, then evaporation, filtration and sublimation
questions.explanation: Gentle heating sublimes the iodine first; water then dissolves the salt, filtration removes the sand and evaporation recovers the salt from the filtrate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A mixture of ethanol (boiling point 78 °C) and water (boiling point 100 °C) is best separated by
questions.explanation: Two miscible liquids with different boiling points are separated by fractional distillation; the more volatile ethanol distils over first.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The coloured dyes in a sample of black ink are best separated by
questions.explanation: Paper chromatography separates the dyes because they travel at different rates up the paper with the solvent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solid melted over the range 108–115 °C instead of sharply at 118 °C, the value given in data tables. The most reasonable conclusion is that the solid
questions.explanation: Impurities lower the melting point and make a solid melt over a range of temperatures; a pure substance melts sharply at a fixed temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas occupies 250 cm³ at 27 °C and 750 mmHg. Its volume at 127 °C and 1000 mmHg is
questions.explanation: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂: V₂ = 250 × (750/1000) × (400/300) = 250 cm³; the effects of the pressure and temperature changes cancel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Under the same conditions, 50 cm³ of hydrogen diffuses through a porous plug in 20 s. The time taken for 50 cm³ of oxygen to diffuse through the same plug is (H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M, so hydrogen diffuses √(32/2) = 4 times as fast as oxygen; oxygen therefore takes 4 × 20 = 80 s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Gas X diffuses 1.5 times as fast as gas Y under the same conditions. If the relative molecular mass of X is 16, that of Y is
questions.explanation: (rate of X ÷ rate of Y)² = M_Y ÷ M_X, so M_Y = 16 × 1.5² = 36.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a sealed metal can containing air is heated, the pressure inside rises because the air molecules
questions.A: become larger and fill more space
questions.B: stick together to form heavier particles
questions.C: increase in number as the air expands
questions.D: move faster and strike the walls more often and harder
questions.explanation: Heating raises the average kinetic energy of the molecules; faster molecules collide with the walls more frequently and with greater force, so the pressure rises.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Under a microscope, pollen grains suspended in water are seen to move in a zig-zag manner. This observation supports the idea that
questions.A: pollen grains are alive and swim
questions.B: pollen grains dissolve slowly in water
questions.D: water molecules are in constant random motion
questions.explanation: Brownian motion of the grains is caused by unequal bombardment by fast-moving water molecules, evidence for the kinetic theory.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume occupied by 0.25 mol of an ideal gas at 27 °C and 1 atm is (R = 0.082 atm dm³ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A cylinder holds 0.1 mol of nitrogen mixed with 0.3 mol of oxygen at a total pressure of 800 mmHg. The partial pressure of the oxygen is
questions.explanation: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure = (0.3/0.4) × 800 = 600 mmHg.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gases is expected to deviate most from ideal behaviour?
questions.explanation: Ammonia molecules are polar and hydrogen-bonded, so the intermolecular forces that the kinetic theory ignores are strongest in ammonia.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes evaporation from boiling?
questions.A: evaporation occurs throughout the liquid; boiling only at the surface
questions.B: evaporation occurs only in closed vessels; boiling in open ones
questions.C: evaporation needs heat; boiling does not
questions.D: evaporation occurs at any temperature; boiling at one fixed temperature
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a surface process that happens at all temperatures, whereas boiling occurs throughout the liquid at the boiling point, when the vapour pressure equals the external pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A fixed mass of gas occupies 600 cm³ at 27 °C. At constant pressure its volume becomes 800 cm³ at

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pressure on a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature is increased from 1 atm to 3 atm. Its volume
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: PV is constant, so tripling the pressure reduces the volume to a third.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The components of crude oil can be separated by fractional distillation because they have different
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates liquids by their boiling points; the fractions condense at different heights in the column.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An atom has mass number 40 and 21 neutrons. The number of electrons in its outermost shell is
questions.explanation: Protons = 40 − 21 = 19 (potassium), configuration 2, 8, 8, 1; there is one electron in the outer shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ion X³⁺ has 10 electrons and 14 neutrons. The mass number of X is
questions.explanation: X³⁺ has lost 3 electrons, so the atom has 13 electrons and 13 protons; mass number = 13 + 14 = 27 (aluminium).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sets of quantum numbers is NOT possible for an electron?
questions.explanation: The value of l can only run from 0 to n − 1, so for n = 3 the largest possible l is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of unpaired electrons in an atom of nitrogen (atomic number 7) is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is 1s² 2s² 2p³; by Hund's rule the three 2p electrons occupy separate orbitals and are all unpaired.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Isotopes of the same element show identical chemical properties because they have the same
questions.explanation: Chemical behaviour depends on the electrons; isotopes differ only in neutron number and hence in mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Neon consists of 90.0% ²⁰Ne, 0.3% ²¹Ne and 9.7% ²²Ne. Its relative atomic mass is approximately

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Boron has a relative atomic mass of 10.8 and consists of the isotopes ¹⁰B and ¹¹B only. The percentage abundance of ¹¹B is
questions.explanation: Let x be the fraction of ¹¹B: 10(1 − x) + 11x = 10.8, so x = 0.8, i.e. 80%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 8 days. The fraction of a sample remaining after 32 days is
questions.explanation: 32 days is four half-lives: 1 → 1/2 → 1/4 → 1/8 → 1/16 of the original amount.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When an atom of ²³⁸₉₂U emits an alpha particle, the daughter nucleus has
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (2 protons, 2 neutrons): the atomic number falls by 2 and the mass number by 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When ¹⁴₆C decays by emitting a beta particle, the product is
questions.explanation: In beta decay a neutron becomes a proton and an electron; the atomic number rises by 1 while the mass number is unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When the radiations from a radioactive source pass between charged plates, the radiation deflected towards the positive plate is
questions.explanation: Beta particles are electrons and carry a negative charge, so they are attracted to the positive plate; alpha particles go the other way and gamma rays are undeflected.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A radioactive sample decays from 80 g to 5 g in 60 minutes. Its half-life is
questions.explanation: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 → 5 is four half-lives, so one half-life = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Rutherford's experiment most alpha particles passed straight through gold foil but a few bounced back. This showed that
questions.A: electrons are heavier than alpha particles
questions.C: gold atoms are mostly solid matter
questions.D: the atom has a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus
questions.explanation: The rare large deflections could only be caused by a very small, massive, positively charged centre, while most of the atom is empty space.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The electronic configuration of the Fe²⁺ ion (Fe, atomic number 26) is
questions.explanation: Iron is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²; the two 4s electrons are lost first, leaving 3d⁶ for Fe²⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following species has the same number of electrons as a neon atom (atomic number 10)?
questions.explanation: Mg²⁺ has 12 − 2 = 10 electrons, the same as neon; Cl⁻ has 18, Na has 11 and F has 9.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Elements P, Q, R and S have atomic numbers 3, 9, 12 and 17 respectively. The pair with similar chemical properties is
questions.explanation: Q (2,7) and S (2,8,7) both have seven outer electrons and are halogens in Group 7; P is a Group 1 metal and R a Group 2 metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Across period 3 from sodium to chlorine the atomic radius decreases because
questions.A: the number of electron shells increases from left to right
questions.B: the atoms lose their outer shells as they become non-metals
questions.C: electrons are progressively removed from the outer shell
questions.D: the nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell
questions.explanation: Each successive element has one more proton pulling on electrons in the same shell, so the shell is drawn closer to the nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following period 3 elements has the highest first ionisation energy?
questions.explanation: Ionisation energy generally rises across a period as nuclear charge increases and the atomic radius shrinks; chlorine is furthest right of the four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element X forms an oxide X₂O₃ which reacts with both acids and alkalis. X is most likely
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃, is amphoteric and aluminium forms X³⁺ ions, giving the formula X₂O₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxide of an element dissolves in water to give a solution of pH 2. The element is most likely
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides such as sulphur(IV) oxide are acidic; metal oxides give neutral or alkaline solutions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Element Y has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 6. Which statement about Y is correct?
questions.A: It is in Group 2 of the periodic table
questions.B: It forms a Y²⁺ ion readily
questions.C: It is a non-metal in period 3
questions.explanation: Three shells place Y in period 3 and six outer electrons in Group 6 (sulphur); it is a non-metal that gains two electrons to form Y²⁻.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Going down Group 1 from lithium to caesium, the reactivity of the metals with water increases because
questions.A: the atoms become smaller and hold water molecules more tightly
questions.B: the number of electrons in the outer shell increases down the group
questions.C: the metals become harder and denser down the group
questions.D: the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more easily lost
questions.explanation: Extra inner shells shield the single outer electron from the nucleus, so less energy is needed to remove it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of elements would combine most readily to form an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: A very reactive metal (Group 1) and a very reactive non-metal (Group 7) transfer electrons readily to form an ionic compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The element with atomic number 20 is found in
questions.explanation: Configuration 2, 8, 8, 2: four shells give period 4 and two outer electrons give Group 2 (calcium).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine displaces bromine from potassium bromide solution, but iodine does not. This shows that the oxidising power of the halogens
questions.C: is the same for all halogens
questions.explanation: A halogen oxidises the ions of those below it in the group; chlorine (above bromine) can, iodine (below bromine) cannot.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following elements is a transition metal?
questions.explanation: Copper forms an ion with a partly filled d-subshell (Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹), the defining feature of a transition metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Iron and copper differ from sodium in that they
questions.A: form coloured ions and show variable oxidation states
questions.C: form only one type of ion
questions.D: have low melting points and densities
questions.explanation: Transition metals typically form coloured compounds (Fe²⁺ green, Cu²⁺ blue) and exist in more than one oxidation state (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Cu⁺/Cu²⁺).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Element X has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 2 and element Y has 2, 7. The compound they form has the formula and bond type
questions.explanation: X loses two electrons to form X²⁺ and each Y gains one to form Y⁻; two Y⁻ ions balance one X²⁺, giving the ionic compound XY₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When hydrogen chloride dissolves in water, H₃O⁺ ions form. The bond between the water molecule and the added proton is
questions.explanation: Oxygen donates both electrons of one of its lone pairs to the proton, which has none; a bond in which one atom supplies both electrons is dative covalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ice floats on water because
questions.A: air bubbles trapped during freezing make the ice lighter than water
questions.B: the molecules in ice are lighter than the molecules in liquid water
questions.C: the covalent O–H bonds become longer and weaker when water freezes
questions.D: hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in an open lattice of lower density
questions.explanation: In ice each molecule is hydrogen-bonded to four others in an open lattice, so ice is less dense than liquid water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not because in graphite
questions.A: each carbon atom bonds to three others, leaving one delocalised electron
questions.B: the carbon atoms are ionised and the ions carry the current
questions.C: the carbon atoms are packed more closely together than in diamond
questions.D: the carbon atoms are held together by metallic bonds instead of covalent bonds
questions.explanation: Each carbon in graphite uses three electrons for bonds within a layer; the fourth is delocalised over the layer and carries current.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A crystal of sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, yet the molten salt conducts well. This is because in the solid
questions.A: there are no ions until the salt melts
questions.B: the sodium and chlorine atoms are covalently bonded
questions.C: all the electrons are shared between the atoms in pairs
questions.D: the ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice
questions.explanation: The ions are present but cannot move in the rigid lattice; once molten or dissolved they are free to move and conduct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The shape of the ammonia molecule, NH₃, is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has three bond pairs and one lone pair; the lone pair pushes the three N–H bonds into a pyramid with a bond angle of about 107°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen fluoride boils at 20 °C while hydrogen chloride boils at −85 °C. The main reason is that
questions.A: HF molecules are held together by hydrogen bonds
questions.B: HF has a higher relative molecular mass
questions.C: HCl is ionic while HF is covalent
questions.explanation: Fluorine is small and very electronegative, so strong hydrogen bonds form between HF molecules and more energy is needed to separate them.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Metals can be hammered into sheets and drawn into wires because
questions.A: the layers of positive ions slide over one another within the sea of electrons
questions.B: their atoms are held together by weak van der Waals forces
questions.D: their bonds break easily and re-form as new compounds
questions.explanation: In metallic bonding the delocalised electrons keep bonding the ions whatever their positions, so layers can slip without the metal shattering.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following substances has a giant covalent structure?
questions.explanation: In SiO₂ every silicon atom is covalently bonded to four oxygens in a continuous network, which is why sand has a very high melting point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following bonds is the most polar?
questions.explanation: Polarity increases with the electronegativity difference between the bonded atoms; fluorine is the most electronegative element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Iodine crystals have a low melting point and sublime easily because
questions.A: only weak van der Waals forces act between the I₂ molecules
questions.B: the covalent bond between the two iodine atoms is very weak
questions.C: iodine is a metal with a weak metallic bond
questions.D: iodine molecules are ionic and the ions separate on heating
questions.explanation: The covalent bond within each I₂ molecule is strong, but the molecules are held to each other by weak intermolecular forces that little heat can overcome.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds contains both ionic and covalent bonds?
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl consists of NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻ ions (ionic), while the N–H bonds inside the ammonium ion are covalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The water molecule is V-shaped (bent) rather than linear because the oxygen atom
questions.A: has two lone pairs of electrons
questions.B: forms a double bond with each hydrogen
questions.explanation: The two lone pairs on oxygen repel the two bond pairs, bending the molecule to an angle of about 104.5°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of 3.01 × 10²³ molecules of water is (H = 1, O = 16, Avogadro's number = 6.02 × 10²³)
questions.explanation: 3.01 × 10²³ molecules is 0.5 mol; 0.5 × 18 = 9.0 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The total number of atoms in 0.2 mol of ammonia, NH₃, is (Avogadro's number = 6.02 × 10²³)
questions.explanation: Each NH₃ molecule has 4 atoms: 0.2 × 4 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 4.8 × 10²³ atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of carbon(IV) oxide at s.t.p. produced when 10 g of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) is heated strongly is (CaCO₃ = 100, molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; 10 g is 0.1 mol, giving 0.1 mol of CO₂ = 0.1 × 22.4 = 2.24 dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The percentage by mass of water of crystallisation in CuSO₄·5H₂O is (Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound has the empirical formula CH₂O and a relative molecular mass of 180. Its molecular formula is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass = 30; 180/30 = 6, so the molecular formula is (CH₂O)₆ = C₆H₁₂O₆.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 0.24 g of magnesium reacts completely with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. The volume of hydrogen produced at s.t.p. is (Mg = 24, molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂; 0.24 g = 0.01 mol Mg gives 0.01 mol H₂ = 0.01 × 22,400 = 224 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 2.4 g of magnesium is burnt in 1.6 g of oxygen. The mass of magnesium oxide formed is (Mg = 24, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO: 0.1 mol Mg needs 0.05 mol O₂, which is exactly the 1.6 g present, so 0.1 mol MgO = 4.0 g forms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 20 cm³ of methane is exploded with 60 cm³ of oxygen. After cooling to room temperature the volume of the gaseous mixture is
questions.explanation: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(l): 20 cm³ CH₄ uses 40 cm³ O₂ and forms 20 cm³ CO₂; the water condenses, leaving 20 cm³ CO₂ + 20 cm³ unused O₂ = 40 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The concentration of a solution containing 5.3 g of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) in 250 cm³ is (Na₂CO₃ = 106)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of water that must be added to 100 cm³ of 0.5 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid to reduce its concentration to 0.2 mol/dm³ is
questions.explanation: C₁V₁ = C₂V₂: 0.5 × 100 = 0.2 × V₂, so V₂ = 250 cm³ and 250 − 100 = 150 cm³ of water must be added.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 8.0 g of copper(II) oxide was reduced by hydrogen and 5.6 g of copper was obtained. The percentage yield of copper is (Cu = 64, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 8.0 g CuO = 0.1 mol, so the theoretical yield is 0.1 × 64 = 6.4 g; 5.6/6.4 × 100 = 87.5%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of moles of ions present when 0.2 mol of calcium trioxonitrate(V), Ca(NO₃)₂, dissolves completely in water is
questions.explanation: Each formula unit gives one Ca²⁺ and two NO₃⁻ ions (three ions): 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the balanced equation aC₃H₈ + bO₂ → cCO₂ + dH₂O, the values of a, b, c and d are respectively
questions.explanation: Propane has 3 C and 8 H, giving 3CO₂ and 4H₂O; the oxygen needed is (6 + 4)/2 = 5 O₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of sodium hydroxide required to prepare 250 cm³ of a 0.1 mol/dm³ solution is (NaOH = 40)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The density of a gas at s.t.p. is 1.25 g/dm³. Its relative molecular mass is (molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: One mole occupies 22.4 dm³ at s.t.p.: 1.25 × 22.4 = 28 (nitrogen or carbon(II) oxide).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas has a vapour density of 22. The volume occupied by 4.4 g of the gas at s.t.p. is (molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass = 2 × vapour density = 44; 4.4 g is 0.1 mol, which occupies 2.24 dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 5.0 g of an impure sample of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) reacted with excess acid to give 896 cm³ of carbon(IV) oxide at s.t.p. The percentage purity of the sample is (CaCO₃ = 100, molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: 896 cm³ = 0.04 mol CO₂, which comes from 0.04 mol = 4.0 g of CaCO₃; 4.0/5.0 × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, the conjugate acid of ammonia is
questions.explanation: A conjugate acid is the base plus one proton; NH₃ gains H⁺ to become NH₄⁺, while water acts as the acid and OH⁻ is its conjugate base.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When the pH of a solution changes from 3 to 5, the hydrogen ion concentration
questions.explanation: pH is −log[H⁺]; each unit is a tenfold change, so two units means [H⁺] falls from 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³, i.e. 100 times.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an acid salt?
questions.explanation: NaHSO₄ still contains a replaceable hydrogen from the parent acid H₂SO₄; it can react with more base to form the normal salt Na₂SO₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution of ammonium chloride turns blue litmus red because
questions.A: the ammonium ion reacts with water to release hydrogen ions
questions.B: the salt contains free hydrochloric acid
questions.D: ammonia gas escapes from the solution
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl is the salt of a strong acid and a weak base; NH₄⁺ hydrolyses (NH₄⁺ + H₂O ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺), making the solution acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 0.1 mol/dm³ solutions of hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid were tested with a pH meter. The hydrochloric acid gave the lower pH because it
questions.A: is more concentrated than the ethanoic acid solution
questions.B: contains chlorine, a very reactive element, while ethanoic acid does not
questions.C: is completely ionised in water while ethanoic acid is only partly ionised
questions.D: has a higher relative molecular mass than ethanoic acid
questions.explanation: At equal concentration the strong acid releases far more H⁺ ions; ethanoic acid exists mainly as un-ionised molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following procedures is most suitable for preparing pure crystals of zinc chloride?
questions.A: mixing zinc with concentrated acid and filtering off the zinc at once
questions.B: burning zinc in chlorine, dissolving the product in water and filtering
questions.C: adding zinc to sodium chloride solution and evaporating to dryness
questions.D: adding excess zinc to dilute HCl, filtering, then evaporating the filtrate to crystallise
questions.explanation: Excess metal ensures all the acid is used; the unreacted zinc is filtered off and the salt crystallises from the filtrate on cooling.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sodium chloride is best prepared in the laboratory by
questions.A: titrating sodium hydroxide with hydrochloric acid and evaporating the neutral solution
questions.B: adding sodium metal to dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.C: adding excess sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) to acid and filtering
questions.D: mixing sodium sulphate and calcium chloride solutions and filtering
questions.explanation: Both reactants and product are soluble, so titration (with an indicator) gives the exact neutral mixture; the salt is then recovered by evaporation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Crystals of Na₂CO₃·10H₂O left in an open dish turn to a white powder after a few days. This process is called
questions.explanation: Efflorescent crystals lose their water of crystallisation to the air and crumble to a powder.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is used to dry chlorine gas because the acid is
questions.explanation: Hygroscopic substances absorb water vapour, so the acid removes moisture from the gas passed through it without reacting with chlorine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide is amphoteric: it forms ZnCl₂ with the acid and sodium zincate, Na₂ZnO₂, with the alkali.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 20 cm³ of 0.25 mol/dm³ tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid exactly neutralised 40 cm³ of potassium hydroxide solution. The concentration of the alkali is
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2KOH → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O: moles of acid = 0.25 × 0.02 = 0.005, so moles KOH = 0.010 in 0.04 dm³ = 0.25 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assuming complete ionisation, the pH of a 0.05 mol/dm³ solution of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is
questions.explanation: Each H₂SO₄ gives two H⁺: [H⁺] = 0.1 mol/dm³ and pH = −log 0.1 = 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The most suitable indicator for the titration of ethanoic acid (a weak acid) with sodium hydroxide is
questions.explanation: The salt formed (sodium ethanoate) is alkaline, so the end point lies above pH 7, in the range where phenolphthalein changes colour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of moles of sodium hydroxide needed to neutralise 1 mol of tetraoxophosphate(V) acid, H₃PO₄, completely is
questions.explanation: H₃PO₄ is tribasic, with three replaceable hydrogens: H₃PO₄ + 3NaOH → Na₃PO₄ + 3H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A few drops of silver trioxonitrate(V) solution added to a salt solution gave a white precipitate that is insoluble in dilute trioxonitrate(V) acid but dissolves in aqueous ammonia. The salt contains
questions.explanation: Silver chloride is a white precipitate that stays in dilute nitric acid but dissolves in ammonia to form a soluble complex ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A salt effervesces with dilute hydrochloric acid, giving a colourless gas that turns lime water milky. The anion present is
questions.explanation: Carbonates (and hydrogencarbonates) release carbon(IV) oxide with dilute acids; the gas forms a white precipitate of CaCO₃ in lime water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A salt solution gives a white precipitate with sodium hydroxide that dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide, and also a white precipitate with aqueous ammonia that dissolves in excess ammonia. The cation is
questions.explanation: Zn(OH)₂ is amphoteric (dissolves in excess NaOH) and also forms a soluble ammine complex in excess ammonia; Al³⁺ and Pb²⁺ do not dissolve in excess ammonia.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of sulphur in sodium thiosulphate, Na₂S₂O₃, is
questions.explanation: 2(+1) + 2x + 3(−2) = 0 gives x = +2 (the average oxidation number of the two sulphur atoms).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O, the oxidising agent is
questions.explanation: Manganese falls from +4 to +2 (it is reduced) while chloride rises from −1 to 0; the substance that is itself reduced is the oxidising agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following changes is an oxidation?
questions.explanation: Oxidation is loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation number; Fe²⁺ loses an electron to become Fe³⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When Cr₂O₇²⁻ is converted to Cr³⁺, the oxidation number of chromium changes from
questions.explanation: In Cr₂O₇²⁻: 2x + 7(−2) = −2, so x = +6; the fall to +3 means chromium is reduced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When chlorine is bubbled through potassium iodide solution, the solution turns brown because
questions.A: chlorine oxidises iodide ions to iodine
questions.B: chlorine dissolves to give a brown solution
questions.C: potassium is displaced as a brown metal
questions.D: chlorine reduces iodide ions to iodine
questions.explanation: Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + I₂; the iodide ions lose electrons (are oxidised) and the iodine formed colours the solution brown.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O, sulphur(IV) oxide acts as
questions.explanation: Sulphur in SO₂ falls from +4 to 0 (reduced) while sulphur in H₂S rises from −2 to 0; SO₂ therefore oxidises H₂S.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a disproportionation reaction?
questions.explanation: In disproportionation the same element is both oxidised and reduced: chlorine goes from 0 to −1 (in NaCl) and to +1 (in NaOCl).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a double decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: Two compounds exchange partners to form two new compounds, one of them a precipitate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Zinc reacts with copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution but copper does not react with zinc tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution. This is because zinc
questions.A: is a stronger reducing agent than copper
questions.B: is a weaker reducing agent than copper
questions.D: has a smaller atomic mass than copper
questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the activity series, so it loses electrons more readily and can displace copper ions from solution, but not the reverse.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, the reducing agent is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen removes oxygen from copper(II) oxide and is itself oxidised to water; the substance oxidised is the reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In acid solution, the number of moles of Fe²⁺ ions oxidised by 1 mol of MnO₄⁻ ions is
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O; manganese gains five electrons, one from each of five Fe²⁺ ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions involves oxidation and reduction?
questions.explanation: Only in the burning of magnesium do oxidation numbers change: Mg goes from 0 to +2 and O from 0 to −2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of nitrogen in the trioxonitrate(V) ion, NO₃⁻, is
questions.explanation: x + 3(−2) = −1 gives x = +5, which is why the ion is named trioxonitrate(V).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When sulphur(IV) oxide is bubbled into acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) solution, the purple colour disappears because SO₂
questions.A: is a bleaching agent for all dyes
questions.B: oxidises the manganese to a colourless compound
questions.C: reduces MnO₄⁻ ions to almost colourless Mn²⁺ ions
questions.explanation: SO₂ is a reducing agent; it is oxidised to sulphate while purple MnO₄⁻ (manganese +7) is reduced to Mn²⁺ (+2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of copper deposited at the cathode when 0.2 faraday of electricity is passed through copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution is (Cu = 64)
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu: 0.2 F deposits 0.2/2 = 0.1 mol = 6.4 g of copper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A current of 3 A passed for 30 minutes through a solution of a divalent metal ion deposited 1.8 g of the metal. The relative atomic mass of the metal is approximately (1 F = 96,500 C)
questions.explanation: Q = 3 × 1800 = 5,400 C = 0.056 mol of electrons; a divalent ion needs 2 mol of electrons per mole, so 0.028 mol of metal weighs 1.8 g, giving M ≈ 64 (copper).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of hydrogen at s.t.p. liberated at the cathode when 0.5 faraday is passed through dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is (molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂: 0.5 F gives 0.25 mol of H₂ = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the electrolysis of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution with copper electrodes, the blue colour of the solution
questions.explanation: Copper dissolves from the anode as fast as it is deposited on the cathode, so the Cu²⁺ concentration, and hence the colour, stays constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When very dilute sodium chloride solution is electrolysed with platinum electrodes, the products at the cathode and anode respectively are
questions.explanation: At low chloride concentration OH⁻ is discharged in preference to Cl⁻, giving oxygen at the anode; H⁺ is always discharged rather than Na⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: To electroplate an iron spoon with silver, the spoon should be made the
questions.A: cathode, in a solution containing silver ions
questions.B: anode, in a solution containing silver ions
questions.C: cathode, in a solution containing iron ions
questions.explanation: Metal is deposited at the cathode (Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag); a silver anode dissolves to keep the Ag⁺ concentration steady.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution, chloride ions are discharged at the anode in preference to hydroxide ions mainly because of
questions.A: the position of chlorine in the electrochemical series
questions.B: the nature of the platinum electrodes
questions.C: the much higher concentration of chloride ions
questions.D: the low temperature of the solution
questions.explanation: Hydroxide ions are normally discharged more easily, but a very high concentration of chloride ions reverses the preference.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Daniell cell Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(aq)||Cu²⁺(aq)|Cu(s), electrons flow through the external wire
questions.explanation: Zinc is oxidised (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻) and releases electrons, which travel through the wire to the copper electrode where Cu²⁺ ions are reduced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The salt bridge in an electrochemical cell
questions.A: supplies electrons to the cathode when the cell is working
questions.B: acts as the negative electrode at which oxidation takes place
questions.C: prevents any ions from moving between the two solutions
questions.D: allows ions to move between the half-cells and keeps them electrically neutral
questions.explanation: Without the salt bridge charge would build up in each half-cell and the current would stop almost immediately.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An iron nail kept in boiled water under a layer of oil did not rust, while a similar nail in tap water open to the air rusted. This shows that rusting requires
questions.explanation: Boiling removes dissolved oxygen and the oil keeps air out; the nail with water but no oxygen did not rust.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A scratched galvanised (zinc-coated) bucket does not rust because zinc
questions.A: forms a waterproof paint over the scratch
questions.C: is more readily oxidised than iron and corrodes in its place
questions.D: reacts with the rust to remove it
questions.explanation: Zinc is above iron in the activity series; it becomes the anode and is sacrificed while iron remains protected even where exposed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V and E°(I₂/I⁻) = +0.54 V, when iron(III) chloride solution is added to potassium iodide solution
questions.D: iodide ions are oxidised to iodine
questions.explanation: E°cell = 0.77 − 0.54 = +0.23 V, so Fe³⁺ oxidises I⁻ to I₂ (the solution turns brown) and is itself reduced to Fe²⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The time needed for a current of 1 A to deposit 0.5 mol of silver from silver trioxonitrate(V) solution is (1 F = 96,500 C)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following liquids will NOT conduct an electric current?
questions.explanation: Sugar dissolves as neutral molecules and gives no ions, so its solution is a non-electrolyte.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When ammonium chloride dissolves in water, the beaker feels cold. This shows that the dissolution is
questions.explanation: Heat is absorbed from the surroundings (the beaker cools), so the enthalpy change is positive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −394 kJ and CO(g) + ½O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −283 kJ, the enthalpy change for C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g) is
questions.explanation: By Hess's law: ΔH = −394 − (−283) = −111 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Bond energies: H–H 436, Cl–Cl 242 and H–Cl 431 kJ/mol. The enthalpy change for H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g) is
questions.explanation: ΔH = bonds broken − bonds formed = (436 + 242) − 2(431) = −184 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 50 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ HCl was mixed with 50 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ NaOH and the temperature rose by 6.8 °C. The enthalpy of neutralisation is (density = 1 g/cm³, c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Heat = 100 × 4.2 × 6.8 = 2,856 J for 0.05 mol of water formed; 2,856/0.05 = 57,120 J/mol ≈ −57.1 kJ/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst added to a reaction does NOT change the
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a lower-energy pathway and speeds up both directions, but the energy difference between reactants and products is unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Raising the temperature increases the rate of a reaction mainly because
questions.A: the activation energy of the reaction is lowered by the heat
questions.B: the molecules become larger and so collide with one another more often
questions.C: more of the molecules have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
questions.D: the reaction becomes more exothermic and releases heat faster
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases the number of molecules with sufficient energy and the collision frequency, so many more collisions are successful.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Food keeps longer in a refrigerator because the low temperature
questions.A: kills all the bacteria in the food
questions.B: stops oxygen from reaching the food
questions.D: slows down the chemical reactions that cause decay
questions.explanation: Rates of reaction, including those catalysed by microbial enzymes, fall sharply as the temperature is lowered.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes is accompanied by an increase in entropy?
questions.explanation: Entropy (disorder) rises when a solid becomes a gas, whose particles move randomly and occupy far more space.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reaction is spontaneous at all temperatures when
questions.A: ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive
questions.B: ΔH is positive and ΔS is negative
questions.C: ΔH and ΔS are both positive
questions.D: ΔH and ΔS are both negative
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is negative at every temperature only when ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an exothermic reaction, the activation energy of the forward reaction is
questions.A: greater than that of the reverse reaction
questions.B: equal to that of the reverse reaction
questions.C: less than that of the reverse reaction
questions.explanation: The products lie below the reactants, so the reverse reaction must climb from a lower level to the same peak, needing more energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The concentration of a reactant fell from 0.8 mol/dm³ to 0.2 mol/dm³ in 3 minutes. The average rate of reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate = change in concentration ÷ time = (0.8 − 0.2)/3 = 0.2 mol dm⁻³ min⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Burning 0.5 g of ethanol raised the temperature of 200 g of water by 15 °C. The enthalpy of combustion of ethanol is approximately (C₂H₅OH = 46, c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A lump of coal burns slowly in air, but coal dust suspended in air can explode. The difference is due to
questions.A: the higher purity of coal dust
questions.B: the much larger surface area of the dust
questions.C: a lower activation energy for coal dust
questions.D: the higher temperature of the dust
questions.explanation: Finely divided solids expose a far greater surface to oxygen, so collisions occur much more often and the reaction is very fast.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), the equilibrium constant Kc is
questions.explanation: Kc = products over reactants, each concentration raised to the power of its coefficient in the balanced equation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Kc for H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) is 50 at a certain temperature. If [H₂] = [I₂] = 0.10 mol/dm³ at equilibrium, the concentration of HI is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which change will shift the equilibrium PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), ΔH = +ve, to the right?
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic, so heat favours it; higher pressure and added Cl₂ push the equilibrium left and a catalyst has no effect on the position.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which statement is true of a chemical system at dynamic equilibrium?
questions.A: the forward and reverse reactions have stopped
questions.B: the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal
questions.C: the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
questions.explanation: Both reactions continue at the same rate, so the concentrations stay constant although they need not be equal to each other.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), a decrease in pressure will
questions.C: have no effect on the equilibrium
questions.explanation: Lower pressure favours the side with more moles of gas; two moles of NO₂ form from one of N₂O₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Changing the pressure has no effect on the position of the equilibrium CO(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO₂(g) + H₂(g) because
questions.A: the reaction is exothermic in the forward direction
questions.B: there are equal numbers of moles of gas on both sides
questions.C: water vapour does not behave as a gas at equilibrium
questions.D: carbon(II) oxide is insoluble in water
questions.explanation: Two moles of gas become two moles of gas, so a pressure change cannot favour either direction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The equilibrium constant of a reaction is 1 × 10¹⁰. This means that at equilibrium
questions.C: reactants and products are present in equal amounts
questions.explanation: A very large K means the numerator (products) is enormous compared with the denominator (reactants); the equilibrium lies far to the right.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Haber process a temperature of about 450 °C is used, although a lower temperature would give more ammonia, because
questions.A: the iron catalyst only works above 450 °C
questions.B: at lower temperatures the rate is too slow to be economical
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic, so low temperature favours the yield, but the compromise temperature gives an acceptable yield quickly enough.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The unit of Kc for the equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) is
questions.explanation: Kc = (mol dm⁻³)² ÷ [(mol dm⁻³)² × (mol dm⁻³)] = 1/(mol dm⁻³) = dm³ mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the equilibrium Fe³⁺(aq) + SCN⁻(aq) ⇌ FeSCN²⁺(aq) (deep red), adding a reagent that removes Fe³⁺ ions makes the red colour fade because
questions.A: the equilibrium shifts to the right to form more FeSCN²⁺
questions.B: the equilibrium shifts to the left to replace the Fe³⁺
questions.C: the FeSCN²⁺ ion is oxidised by the added reagent
questions.D: the SCN⁻ ions are precipitated by the added reagent
questions.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle the system opposes the loss of Fe³⁺ by decomposing some FeSCN²⁺, so less of the red complex remains.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 1 mol of ethanoic acid and 1 mol of ethanol were mixed in a 1 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium 2/3 mol of ethyl ethanoate had formed. The equilibrium constant Kc is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium ester = water = 2/3 mol and acid = alcohol = 1/3 mol: Kc = (2/3 × 2/3)/(1/3 × 1/3) = 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When copper turnings are warmed with concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, a colourless gas is evolved that decolourises acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII). The gas is
questions.explanation: Hot concentrated H₂SO₄ oxidises copper and is itself reduced to SO₂, a reducing gas that decolourises acidified KMnO₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A colourless gas collected over water burns with a 'pop' sound when a lighted splint is brought near it. The gas is
questions.explanation: The pop is the small explosion of hydrogen combining with oxygen in the air to form water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Moist blue litmus paper held in chlorine gas first turns red and is then bleached. The bleaching is caused by
questions.A: chlorine gas dissolving the dye out of the paper
questions.B: oxochlorate(I) acid, formed with the water, which oxidises the dye
questions.C: hydrogen chloride, formed with the water, which reduces the dye
questions.D: the heat released when chlorine reacts with the water
questions.explanation: Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HOCl; the acids turn litmus red and HOCl, an oxidising agent, destroys the colour. Dry chlorine does not bleach.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Freshly prepared iron(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution was added to a salt solution and concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid was poured carefully down the side of the tube. A brown ring formed. The salt contains
questions.explanation: The brown ring test is the confirmatory test for nitrates; the ring is a complex of iron(II) with nitrogen(II) oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid cannot be used to dry ammonia gas because
questions.A: ammonia is insoluble in the concentrated acid
questions.B: the acid reacts with ammonia to form ammonium tetraoxosulphate(VI)
questions.C: the acid is too dilute to absorb the water vapour in the gas
questions.D: ammonia is much lighter than the acid and floats above it
questions.explanation: Ammonia is a base; the drying agent must be non-reactive, so quicklime (CaO) is used instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Brown fumes are produced when concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid is added to copper. The brown gas is
questions.explanation: Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O; nitrogen(IV) oxide is the reddish-brown, acidic gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Graphite is used as a lubricant because
questions.A: it is a very hard substance
questions.B: its layers slide easily over one another
questions.C: it melts at a low temperature
questions.explanation: The weak forces between the flat layers of carbon atoms let the layers slip, so graphite feels slippery.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the extraction of aluminium, purified bauxite (Al₂O₃) is dissolved in molten cryolite. The cryolite is used to
questions.A: act as the reducing agent for the aluminium oxide
questions.B: lower the melting point of the aluminium oxide
questions.C: remove the iron impurities from the aluminium oxide
questions.D: supply extra aluminium ions to the electrolyte
questions.explanation: Alumina melts above 2000 °C; dissolving it in cryolite allows electrolysis at about 950 °C, saving energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Tin is extracted from its ore, cassiterite (SnO₂), by
questions.D: dissolving the ore in acid and evaporating
questions.explanation: Tin is low enough in the activity series for carbon to reduce its oxide: SnO₂ + 2C → Sn + 2CO.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the electrolytic refining of copper, the impure copper is made the
questions.explanation: Copper dissolves from the impure anode as Cu²⁺ and is deposited as pure copper on the cathode; impurities fall as anode sludge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A scratched tin-plated iron can rusts faster than a scratched galvanised iron sheet because
questions.A: tin is more reactive than iron and dissolves away from the scratch
questions.B: tin is less reactive than iron, so the iron corrodes at the scratch
questions.C: zinc forms a barrier that prevents water from reaching the scratch
questions.D: tin reacts with the air to form an acid that attacks the iron
questions.explanation: Once the tin coating is broken, iron (the more reactive metal) becomes the anode and corrodes; zinc, being more reactive than iron, corrodes instead of the iron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sodium metal is stored under paraffin oil because it
questions.A: reacts readily with oxygen and moisture in the air
questions.D: dissolves in water to give an acid
questions.explanation: Sodium tarnishes rapidly in air and reacts violently with water; the oil keeps both away.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A farmer adds quicklime (calcium oxide) to his field in order to
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide is a basic oxide that reacts with acids in the soil, raising the pH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oxygen (O₂) and ozone (O₃) are described as allotropes because they are
questions.B: different physical forms of the same element in the same state
questions.C: compounds of oxygen with different formulae
questions.D: different states of the same substance
questions.explanation: Allotropes are different structural forms of one element, like diamond and graphite for carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nitrogen gas is very unreactive at room temperature because
questions.A: it is a noble gas with a full outer shell of electrons
questions.B: the triple bond between its atoms is very strong
questions.C: its molecules are very large and move very slowly
questions.D: it is less dense than air and escapes before reacting
questions.explanation: Breaking the N≡N bond needs about 945 kJ/mol, so most reactions of nitrogen need high temperature, pressure or a catalyst.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sulphur burns in air with a blue flame to give a gas that turns acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI) paper from orange to green. The gas is
questions.explanation: SO₂ is a reducing agent; it reduces orange dichromate(VI) to green chromium(III).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following hydrocarbons belongs to the alkene series?
questions.explanation: Alkenes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ; C₄H₈ (butene) fits, C₄H₁₀ is an alkane, C₄H₆ an alkyne and C₆H₆ is benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gaseous hydrocarbon decolourises bromine water and gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal silver trioxonitrate(V). It is
questions.explanation: Only a terminal alkyne such as ethyne has an acidic hydrogen that forms the silver salt; ethene decolourises bromine but gives no precipitate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound effervesces with sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) solution. Its functional group is
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to liberate carbon(IV) oxide from hydrogencarbonates; alcohols and aldehydes are not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH=CHCH₃ is
questions.explanation: The chain has four carbons and the double bond starts at the second carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of structural isomers of C₅H₁₂ is
questions.explanation: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are the three isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When ethanol is warmed with acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI), the solution turns from orange to green because
questions.A: ethanol is reduced to ethane while the dichromate(VI) is oxidised
questions.B: ethanol is oxidised while dichromate(VI) is reduced to chromium(III)
questions.C: the orange dichromate(VI) dissolves in the ethanol to give a green solution
questions.D: ethanol is dehydrated to ethene, which reacts with the dichromate(VI)
questions.explanation: Ethanol is oxidised (via ethanal) to ethanoic acid; the oxidising agent Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) is reduced to green Cr³⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent distinguishes ethanol from ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid effervesces with the carbonate, releasing CO₂; ethanol gives no reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When an ester is boiled with sodium hydroxide solution, the products are an alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid. This reaction is called
questions.explanation: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of esters; with fats and oils it produces soap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nylon is formed from its monomers by condensation polymerisation. This means that
questions.A: the monomers simply add together with no other product
questions.B: a small molecule such as water is eliminated as each monomer joins
questions.C: the polymer forms only in the presence of light
questions.D: the monomers must contain a double bond
questions.explanation: In condensation polymerisation each new link releases a small molecule; addition polymers such as polythene form with no by-product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight to form chloromethane and hydrogen chloride. The reaction is
questions.explanation: A hydrogen atom of the saturated alkane is replaced by chlorine; alkanes cannot undergo addition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of oxygen required for the complete combustion of 10 cm³ of propane, C₃H₈, is
questions.explanation: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O; volumes of gases are in the same ratio as moles, so 10 × 5 = 50 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of ethanol obtained by the complete fermentation of 18 g of glucose is (C₆H₁₂O₆ = 180, C₂H₅OH = 46)
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂; 0.1 mol of glucose gives 0.2 mol of ethanol = 0.2 × 46 = 9.2 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds will decolourise bromine water in the dark?
questions.explanation: Only the unsaturated alkene adds bromine across its double bond without light; propane needs light for substitution and benzene resists addition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alcohols is oxidised to a ketone?
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols, in which the –OH carbon carries two alkyl groups, are oxidised to ketones (propanone); primary alcohols give aldehydes and acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound with the molecular formula C₃H₆O₂ could be
questions.explanation: Propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH, has three carbons, six hydrogens and two oxygens; the others contain only one oxygen or more hydrogens.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzene undergoes substitution rather than addition reactions because
questions.A: it has no hydrogen atoms that can be added to or replaced
questions.B: its delocalised electrons give the ring a stability that addition would destroy
questions.C: it is a saturated hydrocarbon with no double bonds at all
questions.D: its carbon atoms are joined by alternating double and single bonds that never move
questions.explanation: The six π electrons are spread over the whole ring; substitution keeps this stable system while addition would break it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethene is converted to ethanol industrially by
questions.B: reaction with steam over a phosphoric acid catalyst
questions.C: heating with concentrated sulphuric acid alone
questions.explanation: Direct hydration: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH at about 300 °C and 60 atm over phosphoric acid on silica.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Permanent hardness in water can be removed by
questions.explanation: Carbonate ions precipitate the Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions as insoluble carbonates; boiling only removes temporary hardness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of hard water?
questions.B: it does not fur kettles and boilers
questions.C: it supplies calcium for strong bones and teeth
questions.explanation: The dissolved calcium salts are nutritionally useful and give the water a pleasant taste; the other options are disadvantages or false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the treatment of water for a town, alum [Al₂(SO₄)₃] is added in order to
questions.A: kill the bacteria and other germs in the water
questions.B: coagulate suspended particles so that they settle
questions.C: remove the hardness caused by dissolved calcium salts
questions.D: add fluoride to the water to protect the teeth
questions.explanation: Alum forms a gelatinous aluminium hydroxide precipitate that traps fine suspended matter; chlorine is added later to kill germs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 100 cm³ of air was passed repeatedly over heated copper until no further change occurred. The volume of gas remaining was about
questions.explanation: Copper removes the oxygen (about 21% of air) as copper(II) oxide, leaving mainly nitrogen, about 79 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rain water collected near an industrial area had a pH of 4.2. This is mainly due to dissolved
questions.B: sulphur(IV) oxide and oxides of nitrogen
questions.explanation: Sulphur and nitrogen oxides from burning fuels dissolve to form sulphurous, sulphuric and nitric acids, making rain far more acidic than the pH 5.6 caused by CO₂ alone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A petrol generator running in a closed room can kill the occupants because it releases
questions.A: carbon(IV) oxide, which is heavier than air and collects near the floor
questions.B: carbon(II) oxide, which binds to haemoglobin and stops oxygen transport
questions.C: nitrogen, which dilutes the oxygen in the room until it cannot be breathed
questions.D: water vapour, which saturates the air and causes suffocation
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion produces odourless carbon(II) oxide, which combines with haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen does.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following wastes is biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Plant material is broken down by bacteria and fungi; plastics, glass and metals persist in the environment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A river water sample has a high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD). This indicates that the water
questions.B: contains a large amount of organic waste
questions.C: has a high concentration of dissolved oxygen
questions.explanation: Bacteria decomposing organic pollution consume dissolved oxygen; the more waste, the more oxygen is demanded.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following observations shows that water is a compound and not a mixture?
questions.A: it boils at 100 °C and freezes at 0 °C at atmospheric pressure
questions.B: electrolysis gives hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio of 2 : 1 by volume
questions.C: it dissolves many substances and is called the universal solvent
questions.D: it can exist as ice, liquid water and steam at different temperatures
questions.explanation: A compound has a fixed composition and can be split into its elements only by chemical means such as electrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A liquid turns white anhydrous copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) blue. This shows that the liquid
questions.explanation: The test detects the presence of water (forming blue CuSO₄·5H₂O) but says nothing about purity; purity is checked by boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a normal component of clean, dry air?
questions.explanation: Sulphur(IV) oxide is a pollutant from burning sulphur-containing fuels; argon (0.9%), CO₂ (0.04%) and nitrogen (78%) are natural constituents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Argon is used to fill electric light bulbs because it
questions.A: glows brightly when the filament heats it
questions.B: is inert and does not react with the hot filament
questions.C: conducts electricity well between the terminals
questions.D: is the cheapest gas available in large quantities
questions.explanation: In air the tungsten filament would oxidise and burn out; the unreactive argon protects it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Soap forms a scum with hard water because the calcium and magnesium ions
questions.A: react with soap to form insoluble salts
questions.B: make the soap dissolve too quickly
questions.C: neutralise the alkali in the soap
questions.D: increase the surface tension of the water
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium stearates are insoluble; soap is wasted as scum until all these ions are removed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Contact process, sulphur(VI) oxide is absorbed in concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid rather than in water because
questions.A: sulphur(VI) oxide is insoluble in water but dissolves in the acid
questions.B: the reaction with water is so violent that it produces a mist of acid droplets
questions.C: water decomposes sulphur(VI) oxide back to sulphur(IV) oxide and oxygen
questions.D: concentrated acid is cheaper and more readily available than pure water
questions.explanation: SO₃ dissolved in 98% H₂SO₄ gives oleum, which is then carefully diluted; direct reaction with water releases too much heat.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The main raw materials for the manufacture of cement are
questions.explanation: Limestone (CaCO₃) and clay (aluminosilicates) are heated in a rotary kiln to form clinker, to which a little gypsum is added.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the fractional distillation of petroleum, the fraction collected at the top of the column is
questions.explanation: The lowest-boiling fraction (methane to butane) rises to the coolest part at the top; bitumen remains at the bottom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Long-chain hydrocarbon fractions from crude oil are cracked mainly because
questions.A: they are too impure to burn cleanly in modern engines
questions.B: the demand for petrol and short-chain alkenes exceeds the yield from distillation
questions.C: long-chain molecules cannot be stored safely in tanks for long periods
questions.D: cracking removes the sulphur compounds that cause acid rain
questions.explanation: Cracking breaks large, less useful molecules into smaller alkanes (petrol) and alkenes (raw materials for plastics).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A petrol that causes little knocking in an engine has a
questions.explanation: The octane number measures resistance to knocking; branched-chain alkanes such as 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (octane number 100) burn smoothly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Most of the ammonia produced by the Haber process is used to make
questions.explanation: Ammonia is converted to ammonium salts and urea, the main nitrogen fertilisers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ordinary glass is made by heating sand (silicon(IV) oxide) with
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ and CaCO₃ react with SiO₂ to form a mixture of sodium and calcium silicates, which cools to soda-lime glass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An advantage of soapless detergents over soap is that they
questions.B: lather well even in hard water
questions.explanation: The calcium and magnesium salts of detergents are soluble, so no scum forms in hard water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A farmer wants to add nitrogen to his soil. Which of the following fertilisers should he use?
questions.explanation: (NH₄)₂SO₄ supplies nitrogen as ammonium ions; the others provide calcium or potassium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.explanation: Bakelite has cross-linked chains and cannot be softened again by heating; the others are thermoplastics that soften on heating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethene, the starting material for polythene and many other petrochemicals, is obtained industrially mainly by
questions.explanation: Cracking naphtha or ethane at high temperature breaks the chains and produces ethene and other alkenes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Solvay process for making sodium trioxocarbonate(IV), the ammonia used is
questions.A: lost as a waste gas through the top of the tower
questions.B: recovered by heating ammonium chloride with calcium hydroxide and re-used
questions.C: converted to ammonium tetraoxosulphate(VI) fertiliser and sold
questions.D: burnt in air to provide the heat needed for the process
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)₂ + 2NH₄Cl → CaCl₂ + 2NH₃ + 2H₂O; recycling the ammonia keeps the process economical.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When starch is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid for some time, the final product is
questions.explanation: Acid hydrolysis breaks starch through dextrins and maltose down to its monomer, glucose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sucrose gives no precipitate with Benedict's solution, but after it is boiled with dilute acid a brick-red precipitate forms. This is because
questions.A: the acid itself is a reducing agent that reacts with the copper(II) ions
questions.B: hydrolysis produces glucose and fructose, which are reducing sugars
questions.C: sucrose is oxidised by the acid to a sugar that reduces copper(II)
questions.D: the heat alone reduces the copper(II) ions in Benedict's solution
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide; acid splits it into two reducing monosaccharides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a protein is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid for several hours, it breaks down into
questions.explanation: Proteins are condensation polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds, which acid hydrolysis breaks.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Fats and oils are esters formed from fatty acids and
questions.explanation: Each glycerol molecule has three –OH groups that combine with three fatty acid molecules to form a triglyceride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A vegetable oil decolourises bromine water but palm kernel fat does not. This shows that the vegetable oil
questions.A: contains more unsaturated fatty acid chains
questions.B: is a saturated fat with no double bonds
questions.C: contains glycerol as well as fatty acids
questions.D: has a higher melting point than the palm kernel fat
questions.explanation: C=C double bonds in the unsaturated chains add bromine; saturated fats have no double bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The white of an egg becomes solid and opaque when boiled because the heat
questions.A: hydrolyses the protein to amino acids
questions.D: removes all the water from it
questions.explanation: Heat destroys the folded structure of albumin so the chains tangle and precipitate; the process is irreversible.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During fermentation with yeast, raising the temperature to 70 °C stops the production of ethanol because
questions.B: the enzymes in the yeast are denatured
questions.D: carbon(IV) oxide is no longer soluble
questions.explanation: Zymase and other enzymes are proteins; above about 60 °C they lose their shape and stop working.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Glucose and fructose both have the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ but different structures. They are described as
questions.explanation: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement are isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Humans cannot digest cellulose although it is made of glucose units, because they
questions.A: lack the enzyme that hydrolyses its β-linkages
questions.B: have no acid in the stomach to break it down
questions.C: cannot absorb the glucose it would produce
questions.D: have too much amylase in their saliva
questions.explanation: Amylase breaks the α-links of starch but not the β-links of cellulose; ruminants rely on bacteria that produce cellulase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Liquid vegetable oils are converted into solid margarine by
questions.explanation: Adding hydrogen across the C=C bonds saturates the chains and raises the melting point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.explanation: Maltose consists of two glucose units joined together; glucose and fructose are monosaccharides and starch a polysaccharide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Amino acids are amphoteric because each molecule contains
questions.A: two acidic carboxyl groups on the same carbon
questions.B: both a basic –NH₂ group and an acidic –COOH group
questions.C: a hydroxyl group attached to a benzene ring
questions.D: a benzene ring with a methyl side chain
questions.explanation: The amino group accepts protons and the carboxyl group donates them, so amino acids react with both acids and bases.
